messages:
pagerduty-bot: P0 alert: multiple auth failures + abnormal token reuse signature on prod-auth-proxy (edge region us-west-2). Trigger: rule 'auth-reuse-heuristic-v2'. Paging on-call.

alice w: I'm on it — grabbing context and starting triage. 

Sanjay Patel: on-call handoff via PD ack. I can join if needed, running quick check on LB logs. Any customer-facing errors?

alice w: Support telemetry shows a small spike in 401s from a handful of customers (approx 0.6% of requests) between 09:14 and 09:18 UTC. No 5xxs. Looks like repeated token reuse and short bursts from ~54.85.12.0/24 and ~43.210.5.0/24.

Maya Chen: @alice w can you paste the raw probe sample? also tagging @security-bot for keys/cred context.

alice w: Pasting sample log (sanitized):
```
2026-03-15T09:15:11Z auth-proxy request_id=abc123 user_id=usr_42 src=54.85.12.37 auth_type=bearer status=401 reason=invalid_token token_sig=eyJhb... reused_count=8
2026-03-15T09:15:12Z auth-proxy request_id=abc124 user_id=usr_42 src=54.85.12.37 auth_type=bearer status=200 matched_token=eyJhb...
```
Note: same token_sig observed across different sessions and IPs.

security-bot: Flagging as "possible token replay / session binding bypass". Recommend immediate scoped mitigation: denylist offending IP ranges at edge and issue emergency rotation for any service tokens identified. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/auth-replay

Leo Rivera: I'll push an edge denylist rule for the two CIDR blocks now (short-lived). Applying WAF block at us-west-2 edge.

Sanjay Patel: Confirmed: WAF rule applied (rule id: wf-98431). We'll monitor for fallback traffic. Also enabling additional logging on auth-proxy for token binding headers.

alice w: Noted. @support-lead please prepare a brief customer comms template in case we have to alert customers whose tokens were observed. Right now it's limited but we should be ready.

support-lead: Drafting a template, will post in #support-escalations in 15m. Suggest no public blast yet, wait for key rotation confirmation.

Maya Chen: Running quick backend scan for leaked logs containing bearer tokens. Querying S3 access logs and Cloudwatch for patterns of 'Authorization: Bearer' exposures in recent 48h.

security-bot: If any S3 objects return matches, tag as sensitive and schedule immediate object re-encryption and access revocation. Also check Vault/KMS audit for any recent downloads of service tokens.

alice w: Found one suspicious internal CI job that printed env AUTH_TOKEN to logs around 03:02 UTC. Object path: s3://redwood-ci/logs/job-9081/step-3.txt — marking as suspected leak.

Maya Chen: Confirmed. That token appears expired, but may have been reused by attacker. We need to rotate any long-lived tokens that could reference the same key material.

security-bot: Action items: 1) Rotate all service tokens associated with CI job-9081 (scope: CI-runner service account). 2) Rotate any API keys that show reuse patterns. 3) Roll temporary denylist for suspicious IPs. 4) Legal/Privacy notified if customer tokens involved.

Sanjay Patel: I'm starting token rotation for CI-runner service account. Will push new creds and update CI variables. Estimated 10 min.

Leo Rivera: Edge denylist holding. Saw ~90% reduction in reuse events. Some retries from different ASNs — expanding monitoring.

alice w: Observed two customer session tokens (masked) in the leaked CI log. Opening an incident window for potential customer impact. @support-lead we need a list of affected customer IDs and a recommended remediation (force logout, rotate tokens).

support-lead: Pulling list now. Will prepare targeted notifications and an internal FAQ for CS reps.

Maya Chen: Rotation plan in progress:
- Step 1: rotate CI-runner service account tokens (in progress by @Sanjay Patel)
- Step 2: invalidate tokens observed in logs (force-expire session IDs)
- Step 3: issue short-lived emergency key rotation for any tokens that had reuse_count > 5
- Step 4: run downstream compatibility smoke tests for ingestion and auth flows

Sanjay Patel: CI-runner rotation completed. New creds pushed and CI env updated. Verified jobs succeed on test branch.

security-bot: Confirming rotation of CI-runner creds and marking old tokens as revoked in Vault (revocation id: rev-20260315-01).

alice w: Force-expire observed session tokens and schedule logout for affected session ids (list posted to secure docs).

Maya Chen: KMS audit shows no external downloads of vault-encrypted keys. It looks scoped to leaked log content rather than KMS compromise.

support-lead: Customer list compiled: three customers with low traffic exposure window. Draft sent to #support-escalations. Recommending targeted PM and action items: rotate customer tokens server-side, force re-auth where possible, and offer incident summary.

alice w: Escalating to Incident Commander: @Maya Chen will take IC. Objectives: contain, assess customer impact, coordinate rotation and comms.

Maya Chen: Taking IC. Logging incident in tracker: INC-2026-0315-01. ETA for initial postmortem: 72h. Will coordinate with legal if required.

security-bot: Please capture the following in the incident timeline: detection at 09:14 UTC, WAF denylist applied 09:16 UTC, CI-runner rotation 09:22 UTC, customer token invalidation 09:28 UTC.

Leo Rivera: Leaving short-term monitor on alerting channels. Will hand back to on-call after 30m.

alice w: Handoff: @Sanjay Patel will remain responsible for edge mitigations; @Maya Chen is IC for the rest. Marking thread as active incident.

Sanjay Patel: Will continue watch. Not seeing new reuse after block, but expanding regex scanning and adding a temporary alert threshold lower to catch slow probes.

support-lead: I'll queue a scheduled status update to affected customers in 1h unless we have new info.

Maya Chen: Next steps for post-triage: full log sweep for other CI jobs, update runbook with detection signature improvements, and a short retro to tighten logging hygiene (no raw tokens in logs).

alice w: Great work team. If any new suspicious activity shows up tag this thread and @security-bot. Closing active paging loop; incident remains active for follow-ups. :lock:
